text:
incident-bot: [PagerDuty] Trigger: high error-rate detected on /v1/generate. Service: redwood-inference-prod-monitoring. Page sent to: infra-oncall@redwood (response window 3m). 
ana patel: ugh, that service name looks wrong — should be routed to runtime-oncall, not infra. did pd remap names last deploy? :thinking_face:
mike chen: I got the page. I'm infra but this is an inference runtime error (lots of 500s on generation). forwarding to runtime oncall.
liam o'connor: acknowledging. Thanks for the heads up. Can someone drop the request ids? need to correlate logs.
sarah nguyen: here's a sample request id from the alert payload: req_9f2b1c. Logs show KV cache flush failed, then OOM on worker-3.
julia (sre): copying trace: `2026-03-14T21:08:12Z worker-3 OOM while allocating kv-cache (seq 1024)`
mike chen: so infra got paged because PD service name was `redwood-inference-prod-monitoring` which matches an old binding to infra-oncall. runtime team uses `redwood-inference-runtime`.
liam o'connor: has runtime been bound to correct PD service? I'll check the rotation.
pagerduty-bot: Incident 324891 auto-created: "High error rate /v1/generate" — routed to redwood-inference-prod-monitoring (service ID svc_45a). Assigned: infra-oncall (escalation policy infra-ep).
nana patel: this is a bad route for customer-impacting generation errors. customers using hosted API get 502s. we need immediate fix (re-route) and then a postmortem on routing rules.
mike chen: for immediate mitigation, I've run a manual re-route: `pd call-route svc_45a --to svc_9b2 (redwood-inference-runtime)` — can someone confirm PD accepted it?
pagerduty-bot: Call-route request submitted by mike chen. Status: pending approval (requires 2 approvals).
julia (sre): I can't approve PD changes from mobile. liam can you approve?
liam o'connor: approve.
pagerduty-bot: Change approved by liam o'connor. Re-route executed. New assignment: runtime-oncall.
liam o'connor: runtime team taking over. investigating OOM cause; temporarily scaled up worker pool and rolled a config that increases KV cache eviction.
sarah nguyen: after the scale up, error rate dropped by ~70% and customer-facing 502s stopped. Confirmed mitigation working.
nana patel: thanks. now the follow-up: PD config had two similarly named services which caused human confusion and an old binding to infra. we need a permanent fix: rename old monitoring service, tighten PD service tags, and add automated test that simulates a runtime error to validate routing.
julia (sre): created ticket INF-2026: "PagerDuty service name collision — enforce unique naming and tag-based routing". assigned to platform team, priority P1 for this quarter.
mike chen: also adding a quick guard: runbook step to verify service->escalation mapping at deploy time. I'll open PR with a predeploy check.
liam o'connor: recorded handoff notes in incident doc and pinged customer success — CS notified of customer impact window (21:07–21:22 UTC) and affected tenants list.
sarah nguyen: leaving a technical note: suspected cause was an aggressive KV cache retention combined with a recent model seq-length bump; will add an entry to runtime tuning doc.
nana patel: good. post-incident actions: 1) rename pd service, 2) add automated routing test, 3) predeploy mapping check, 4) update runbook and alert thresholds, 5) notify customers and compile RCA.
liam o'connor: closing the live page; monitoring for 30m, will reopen if error rate > 2% for more than 5m.
incident-bot: Incident 324891 status: resolved -> monitoring. All pages acknowledged.
mike chen: thanks everyone. quick retro tomorrow 10:00 to decide permanence of KV settings. :thumbsup:
